Events have been an important approach for companies to attract leads and make conversions. Event organizers leverage the events platform at LinkedIn to create event pages where members can register to attend events, join live stream online events, and participate in the post-event activities. At the same time, attendees discover relevant events, make new connections, and nurture existing relationships on the platform.
Access to the LinkedIn Marketing API Program doesn't automatically grant access to the following APIs. Developers must apply separately to be considered for these APIs.

An event cannot be updated until it has been posted. Events are updated using a partial update request (POST with X-RestLi-Method: partial_update). The last component of the URL path is the ID of the event to update.
Not all event fields can be updated after creation. The following table summarizes the three mutability categories:

Rows.Text: id, created, lastModified, ugcPost, leadGenForm, type.online.format.liveVideo.liveVideo
Never settable by partners. Any attempt to include these in a partial update is rejected.
organizer, type (online vs. in-person discriminator), type.online.format (liveVideo or external discriminator), leadGenFormSpec, type.online.format.liveVideo.testEvent
Can be set at creation but cannot be changed afterward. Do not include these fields in partial updates to change their value.
name, description, vanityName, startsAt, backgroundImage, discoveryMode, and type sub-fields: endsAt, url, address, venueDetails
Can be changed after creation, subject to the lifecycle restrictions below.

Blocks.Text: Note
From API version 202605 and later, hasDarkUgc is also a CREATE ONLY field.
The lifecycle state of an event determines whether any update is permitted:

Rows.Text: All updatable fields can be updated.
No fields can be updated. Returns HTTP 400: Event cannot be modified once it has started.
No fields can be updated. Returns HTTP 403: No updates can be made to cancelled event.

Blocks.Text: Note

The "started" check is based solely on whether the original startsAt has passed. This restriction applies to all fields, not just time-related fields. Attempting to update name, description, or any other field after this time will result in an HTTP 400 error.
The following examples update all updatable fields. Replace the event id, timestamps, and field values with your own. The type sub-fields available depend on the event type:

In-person:

type.inPerson.endsAt
type.inPerson.url
type.inPerson.address
type.inPerson.venueDetails


External online:

type.online.format.external.endsAt
type.online.format.external.url


Live video:

type.online.format.liveVideo.endsAt
Note

The type discriminator (inPerson vs online) is CREATE ONLY and cannot be changed after creation.
When including type in a partial update, the member key in the patch (inPerson, online) must match the event's existing type. Use it only to update nested sub-fields such as endsAt, url, address, and venueDetails.
Do not attempt to change the type discriminator.

POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/events/7246559654799892480
X-RestLi-Method: partial_update
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
